title: Majority illusion drives the spontaneous emergence of alternative states in common-pool resource games with network-based information

key_points.claim: An agent-based model is used to study how social network structure shapes common-pool resource (CPR) extraction; the ABM is of a stylized artificial population of resource users.
key_points.evidence_quote: We use an agent-based model to investigate how social networks shape resource extraction outcomes.

key_points.claim: Highly visible network nodes create a 'majority illusion' that misleads agents about the dominant behavior. This can push the whole population into one of two states, either abundant/high-welfare or depleted/low-welfare.
key_points.evidence_quote: This misperception can push the entire population toward one of two possible states: an abundant, high-welfare resource or a depleted, low-welfare one.

key_points.claim: Aligning users' environmental impact with their visibility reduces bistability and leads to a single, predictable outcome.
key_points.evidence_quote: Aligning users’ environmental impact with their visibility can mitigate this effect and steer the system toward a single, predictable outcome.

key_points.claim: Policy implication: reshaping information flows, particularly by targeting high-impact hubs, could stabilize cooperation and reduce tragedy-of-the-commons risk.
key_points.evidence_quote: network-based policies, such as reshaping information flows, particularly targeting high-impact hubs, could help stabilize cooperative behaviors

key_points.claim: Highlights: information asymmetry produces bistability. A few key users drive it, and which outcome occurs depends on the stochastic emergence of those users' behavior.
key_points.evidence_quote: The stochastic emergence of key users’ behavior determines which outcome results

reliability_notes: Full text was fetched (about 96k characters), but I read only the abstract, highlights and the start of the introduction. Quotes come from those parts. Peer-reviewed, open access, 2025. I did not extract model details such as parameters, network types and payoff structure. The paper is a narrow CPR-game ABM, not a broad survey of artificial societies.
